parts.name: Homepage
parts.description: We follow one visitor from the homepage, into the client portal, down to the database and over to the staff side. Each number marks a part of the page; colors show which layer of the software it belongs to.

parts.name: Accounts
parts.description: How a visitor becomes a client: registration, email confirmation and signing in.

parts.name: Client dashboard
parts.description: What a signed-in client sees first, and how the page makes sure each client only ever sees their own data.

parts.name: A process
parts.intro: Part 4: A process, step by step
parts.description: What happens when a client starts a service and uploads documents: the core of Galiel.

parts.name: Alerts and news
parts.description: How Galiel keeps clients informed without anyone sending messages by hand.

parts.name: The staff side
parts.description: The other half of Galiel: how the team manages every process from one back office.

stops.title: A ready-made homepage
stops.body: The public homepage is a finished HTML file. The web server sends it as is, so it loads instantly and needs no database.

stops.title: Three languages
stops.body: Every label exists in English, Spanish and French. A small script swaps the words in the browser, without reloading the page.

stops.title: Routing: one address, one function
stops.body: Each web address points to one Python function. "Find a service" opens /services/, which runs the catalog view and decides what this visitor may see.

stops.title: How the catalog is stored
stops.body: Locations are a hierarchy: country → state → city. Each service is offered in a specific place, with its own requirements and documents.

stops.title: Sign in and security
stops.body: Passwords are stored hashed, never as plain text. New accounts must confirm their email, and every private page checks who is signed in before showing anything.

stops.title: The design layer
stops.body: Pages are HTML templates styled with CSS. The signature is a vector drawing animated stroke by stroke, and the moving banner stops for people who prefer less motion.

stops.title: The trip of one click
stops.body: The browser asks Apache. Apache hands the request to Django through FastCGI. Django reads SQLite, fills a template and sends the finished page back.
stops.tech: HostGator Linux · Apache · FastCGI · Django 4.2 · SQLite

stops.title: How it was built
stops.body: Agile: short rounds, each ending in a working release. 99 automated tests run on every change, and every release had a backup and a one-command undo.
stops.tech: GitHub Actions · 99 tests · dry-run, backup, rollback

stops.title: Registration creates two records
stops.body: Submitting the form creates a User (login and hashed password) and, automatically, a Profile with phone, company and language. The account starts inactive.

stops.title: Email activation
stops.body: Galiel emails a one-use link with a signed token. Clicking it activates the account; an old or altered link is rejected.

stops.title: Sign in remembers what you wanted
stops.body: If a visitor picked a service before signing in, the login view remembers it and continues there; otherwise it opens the dashboard.

stops.title: One shared workspace frame
stops.body: Every portal page reuses the same header, draft banner and 01–09 tabs from one base template, so a change is made once and appears everywhere. On phones the tabs become a swipeable row.

stops.title: Counts that only see your data
stops.body: Each number is a database query filtered by the signed-in client. A client can never count, or see, another client’s processes or files.

stops.title: Processes and the GAL number
stops.body: Each process gets a readable number (GAL-000006) and a status. The banner on top always points to the next unfinished step.

stops.title: A scripted help assistant (no AI)
stops.body: The ? button offers fixed questions. Answers come from the catalog and from this client’s own processes, never from anyone else’s.

stops.title: Starting a process
stops.body: Choosing a service creates a ServiceApplication in Draft and logs its first event. The process then moves through six numbered steps.

stops.title: Six steps with autosave
stops.body: Answers are saved in the background as the client types, so nothing is lost. Once staff send a quote, the answers lock and can no longer change.

stops.title: Every upload is checked
stops.body: The server reads the first bytes of each file to confirm it is really a PDF, JPG or PNG, and rejects anything over 10 MB, even if the name says .pdf.

stops.title: Files kept outside the website
stops.body: Uploaded files are saved in a private folder that the web server cannot publish. They download only through a view that checks login and ownership.

stops.title: A status with a history
stops.body: A process moves from Draft to Ready through 11 statuses. Every change is recorded with who and when, so clients and staff see the same timeline.

stops.title: The bell
stops.body: The bell asks the server for the number of unread alerts and shows it as a small count. It is a tiny view that returns only that number.

stops.title: Alerts create themselves
stops.body: When staff change a process to “Missing documents” or “Quote ready”, a signal creates an alert for that client in three languages. Nobody writes it by hand.

stops.title: Daily jobs on the server
stops.body: Every morning a scheduled job sends email copies for due dates; every night another backs up the database and client files, keeping 14 days.

stops.title: News & updates
stops.body: Staff post announcements with titles in English, Spanish and French, a publish date and an expiry date. Expired or future news never shows.

stops.title: The staff back office
stops.body: Staff manage clients, services, prices and processes from Django’s built-in admin, customized for Galiel. Clients can never open it.

stops.title: One change, three effects
stops.body: Setting the status to “Missing documents” and saving creates the client’s alert, emails a copy, and re-opens uploads for that client.

stops.title: Clear roles
stops.body: Staff and clients are separate roles. Staff cannot create client applications, and clients cannot see staff pages or other clients’ data.

stops.title: Conversations
stops.body: Each process can have one conversation thread between the client and staff, so every question stays attached to its case.
